short: The third khagan, whose two-year reign ended as he marched to fight his cousin Batu.
full:
Ögedei's death in 1241 left his widow Töregene as regent for five years while she manoeuvred to have her eldest son elected. Güyük was raised on the shield at a kurultai on the Orkhon on 24 August 1246, before an assembly that included Rus' princes, Seljuk and Georgian claimants, and the Franciscan Giovanni da Pian del Carpine, who carried a papal letter urging the khan to accept baptism and stop killing Christians.

Güyük's reply, which survives in Persian in the Vatican archives, told Innocent IV to come in person and submit. At home he reversed his mother's appointments, executed her favourite Fatima, and ordered an empire-wide census. He had never forgiven Batu for slights during the Hungarian campaign, and in 1248 marched west with an army, ostensibly for his health. Batu moved to meet him. Güyük died on 20 April, aged about forty-two, before the two forces made contact — plausibly of drink and illness, though poison was suspected. The throne stayed empty for three more years.
